newsitem.title: USA: UPS labor pact increases full-time jobs.
newsitem.headline: UPS labor pact increases full-time jobs.

text.p: A tentative labor agreement between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union that ended a 15-day strike included the following provisions, the union and company said on Tuesday.
-- New labor contract is for five years.
-- Conversion of 10,000 part-time jobs into full-time positions. The company had earlier offered to add only 1,000 more full-time jobs.
-- UPS dropped a proposal to start a new company-controlled pension plan that would have shifted contributions from the Teamsters multi-employer pension plans.
-- Use of subcontractors, except during holiday peak periods, is phased out over six months. Those jobs would go to UPS workers.

-- Increase in hourly wage rates by up to about 36 percent. Full-time workers gain $3.10 an hour over five years and part-time workers gain $4.10. Top-rate full-time employees will eventually be paid $23 an hour and top-rate part-time worker pay will rise to about $15 from $11 an hour.
-- An increase in the UPS package weight limit must be negotiated with the union.
The company said job cuts were likely, predicting a 5 percent loss of business that may result in the loss of 15,000 jobs.
Union members must ratify the settlement.
